$comment: D-FFI-IOCTL-SIZE-FIELD-OVERFLOW-SILENT — the ELF half of the per-format SIZE CEILING now carried inside the shipped <sys/ioctl.h> request-encoding macros, and the only place a boundary encoding goes through the RELEASE optimizer and out across a real variadic libc `ioctl`. THE DEFECT: musl's `_IOC` does not mask the length (`sizeof(t) << 16`, verbatim in `src/dss-config/shippedLibs/sys/ioctl.json`'s elf arms), so at `sizeof(t) >= 0x4000` bit 30 lit up and the size collided with the 2-bit DIRECTION field — a 0x4000-byte `_IOR` encoded as 0x80000000|0x40000000, which IS `_IOWR`, i.e. the kernel copying the argument the WRONG WAY, with no diagnostic anywhere. Darwin's arm overflows the OTHER way (it MASKS to 13 bits, so 8192 bytes encodes size ZERO), which is why the ceiling is PER-FORMAT and lives in the same `when:{format}` arms as the encodings. ★ THE SPLIT IS THE POINT, AND IT IS A TYPE THIS PROGRAM ACTUALLY PASSES TO A SYSCALL: `struct DssIoctlSplitArg` is 8192 bytes — one past Darwin's IOCPARM_MASK (8191), less than half of Linux's _IOC_SIZEMASK (16383) — so the SAME declaration this file compiles, links and runs is REFUSED at compile time on macho. No single global ceiling and no engine branch could produce both answers. ★ WHAT THIS ADDS OVER tests/ffi/test_shipped_ioctl_size_ceiling.cpp, which already pins both formats on every host: that test drives the FRONT END and stops at the compile verdict; this one carries the boundary encodings through the release optimizer and the real `unsigned long` request parameter, so a fold that is right in the constant evaluator and wrong after optimization has somewhere to fail. THE REFUSAL HALF IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT HERE — a corpus example asserts a successful build and an exit code, and `examples/` has no compile-failure convention, so `a 16384-byte type must NOT compile` is pinned in the unit test and nowhere else. VALUES, all published Linux/asm-generic encodings with 0xf5 = F2FS_IOCTL_MAGIC (the magic sqlite itself writes on this arm): at the ceiling _IOR=0xbffff50c, _IOW=0x7ffff50d, _IOWR=0xfffff50e; at the split size _IOR=0xa000f50c; and at sqlite's own 32-byte scale _IOR=0x8020f50c, which is the control that the ceiling moved NOTHING. The three direction fields are also read back explicitly (`>> 30` == 2/1/3) rather than left to the whole-word compare, because an oversized length bleeding into those two bits is exactly the defect. Plus the forward sign-extension guard the sibling examples carry: `_IOWR` at the ceiling has its top TWO bits set, and it must widen into the request parameter by ZERO extension. BOTH elf arches are listed deliberately — a macro variant's `when` is FORMAT-only by construction, so x86_64 and arm64 MUST agree, and this is the witness for that claim. HOST REALITY: elf-only targets with runOn linux, so a Windows or macOS host COMPILES both arms (every value pin is a compile-time _Static_assert, load-bearing there) and reports SkippedCrossHost for the run; the Linux legs run `main`. exit 42 iff every boundary encoding survived the optimizer AND the direction field stayed its own. RED-ON-DISABLE, stated precisely so it is not mistaken for more than it is: deleting the ceiling term from the elf arms leaves this file GREEN — correctly, since removing a ceiling cannot change a value under it, and that removal is caught by the unit test's refusal arm. What this file catches is a guard that stops contributing zero, or a ceiling copy-pasted from the macho arm; both turn the asserts RED.
